detail: Full summary: claude-context's own evaluation undercuts semantic-code-search hype: on 30 SWE-bench Verified instances (GPT-4o-mini), retrieval F1 was IDENTICAL to a bare read/grep/edit baseline (0.40 vs 0.40); the only measured win was token efficiency (73,373→44,449, -39.4%) and fewer tool calls. Relevant if anyone proposes adding semantic code search to Twining's scope — the quality claim doesn't survive its own benchmark; the win is cost, and only at large-unfamiliar-codebase scale.
